channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7807 vs. 6.7829 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.7807 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7829 and 6.7167 Reuters estimate.

item.title: British Pound consolidates near three-week low as Fed bets and Iran tensions support USD
item.description: The GBP/USD pair consolidates below the 1.3500 psychological mark during the Asian session on Thursday and remains close to a three-week low, touched the previous day.

item.title: Euro steadies below 1.1600 as hawkish Fed rhetoric limits gains
item.description: The EUR/USD pair holds steady near 1.1590 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and escalating conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: US President Donald Trump: Renewed campaign against Iran will not continue for too long
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that while the US is prepared to strike Iran again at any time, he doesn’t expect the renewed fighting to last “too long,” Reuters reported on Wednesday.

item.title: The Australian Dollar's thirteen-year high is a New Zealand story
item.description: AUD/NZD spent Wednesday pushing at a ceiling that has held since 2013, running from near 1.2100 to a high short of 1.2300 and trading just above 1.2250 into the European afternoon.

item.title: Gold rebounds above $4,350 as US Dollar, Treasury yields slip
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rebounds from a nearly one-month low to around $4,385 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal edges higher as the ‌US Dollar (USD) and Treasury yields retreat from recent highs.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Sellers eye 214.00 after SMA break
item.description: The Pound Sterling collapses versus the Japanese Yen as growing “speculation” of an intervention in the FX markets witnessed the Yen appreciating versus most G8 FX currencies. The GBP/JPY trades with losses of more than 1.10%, at 214.08.

item.title: The New Zealand Dollar sells the hike it asked for
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) raised its policy rate on Wednesday and the currency fell almost 1.7% from top to bottom on the day it happened.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises as soft US jobs, GDP beat lift AUD, PMIs ahead
item.description: The Australian Dollar advanced on Wednesday versus the US Dollar after economic data in the US revealed the labour market weakened slightly, while the Greenback dipped on intervention speculation in the FX markets.

item.title: Intervention buys the Japanese Yen less ground every time
item.description: The Yen had its best session in weeks on Wednesday and it still looks like a losing position.

item.title: Rising gilt yields are not saving the British Pound
item.description: Sterling has spent Wednesday handing back the last of its August rally, with GBP/USD trading just under 1.3500 after a session low a shade beneath 1.3475.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls eye 0.8200 as RSI turns higher
item.description: The USD/CHF pair advances some 0.13% on Wednesday as the Greenback holds within familiar levels, after depreciating versus the Japanese Yen amid speculation of an intervention in the FX markets. This dragged the pair from around five-week highs to the 0.8120 area.

item.title: Gold rises as speculation of Yen intervention weighs on the US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price rises over 1% on Wednesday as the Greenback softens amid speculation of an intervention to bolster the Japanese Yen (JPY), while US Treasury yields hold firm after weak US jobs data. At the time of writing, the XAU/USD pair trades at $4,373.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strong exports and BoK stance back gradual KRW gains – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights that South Korea’s export boom and a large trade surplus, combined with a hawkish Bank of Korea, are supportive for the Korean Won. They argue that changing FX flow dynamics should allow more of the surplus to translate into KRW strength.

item.title: US President Trump says Iran campaign “won’t last”, warns of more strikes
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the renewed campaign against Iran “won’t continue for too long," adding that he is prepared to launch another attack on Iran.

item.title: Fed’s Beige Book shows modest economic growth as prices rise
item.description: The Federal Reserve (Fed) released its Beige Book on Wednesday, in which the US central bank stated that economic activity increased modestly since early July, while overall employment rose slightly. Regarding inflation, prices rose in eight districts.

item.title: WTI Oil fluctuates near six-week high as Middle East tensions fuel volatility
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil sees two-way price swings on Wednesday as escalating tensions in the Middle East keep energy markets volatile and the geopolitical risk premium elevated.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Higher oil prices add to IDR pressure - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan remains cautious on the Indonesian Rupiah as domestic inflation accelerates and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth stays above 5%. The trade balance has improved slightly but remains weaker than 2025 averages due to higher Oil and gas imports.

item.title: Forex Today: Weekly claims and ISM Services keep the focus on the real economy
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has traded in quite a volatile fashion on Wednesday, always amid the unabated tensions from the US-Iran crisis, speculation over another bout of FX intervention by Japanese authorities and bets for whatever the Fed might do or not do in the next few months.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downside risks remain against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that USD/SGD is rebounding alongside a stronger US Dollar (USD), supported by higher US Treasury yields and firmer Fed hike expectations.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average borrows its rebound from the bond market
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 53,000 and roughly 250 points higher, having opened just above 52,750, dipped to a session low beneath the rising 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) near 52,700, and recovered the whole of that ground.

item.title: British Pound: Break below 1.35 shifts focus lower against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret describe GBP/USD as soft but mid-pack within the G10, with domestic data and Bank of England (BoE) events limited ahead of Governor Bailey’s speech.

item.title: British Pound hits three-week low as US yields, Iran risks weigh
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) falls by some 0.11% and hits a three-week low against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, even though the US Dollar Index (DXY) is in red territory, following US jobs data that were below estimates but signaled some cooling in the labor market.

item.title: BoC recap: Risks are shifting as Oil prices and US trade actions complicate outlook
item.description: The Bank of Canada (BoC) left its overnight interest rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday, as widely anticipated, but delivered a more cautious message as inflation risks increased and the recovery became harder to assess.

item.title: Indian Rupee: September gains face structural tests – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists highlight that the Indian Rupee’s (INR) strong start to September is reflected in a move back below the 100dma, raising questions about whether Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention has helped the currency turn a corner despite a hawkish Fed and higher Oil prices.

item.title: Gold turns positive as turmoil in Yen pairs hits US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) stages a sharp rebound on Wednesday, reversing all its earlier losses as a sudden rise in the Japanese Yen (JPY) triggers broad selling pressure on the US Dollar (USD). A pullback in US Treasury yields provides additional support to the precious metal.

item.title: United States Dollar Index loses ground on possible Yen intervention
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades on the back foot on Wednesday as a sharp rise in the Japanese Yen (JPY) forces the Greenback to reverse its earlier intraday gains. At the time of writing, DXY trades around 99.55, down 0.11% on the day, after reaching 99.86, its highest level since August 14.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks build against US Dollar as oil rises – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note EUR/USD has slipped to the upper 1.15s, with sentiment turning bearish despite supportive yield spreads. They link the renewed deterioration to rising Oil prices and concerns over Euro area terms of trade.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Strong GDP and carry support – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes AUD/USD fell toward 0.7125 on broad US Dollar (USD) strength, even as Australia’s Q2 GDP beat expectations at 0.4% q/q and 2.1% y/y.

item.title: Euro tumbles against the Yen as intervention fears hit crosses
item.description: The Euro (EUR) tumbles against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Wednesday amid growing speculation that Japanese authorities may have intervened in the FX markets, as most Yen pairs collapsed to fresh two-week lows, with EUR/JPY bottoming at around 183.64 from a daily high of 185.75.
